raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

`MXFP8Tensor.quantize_()` accepts caller-provided unswizzled `scale_inv` buffers, including compact ones that hold one scale per block (`(rows, cols/32)` rowwise, `(rows/32, cols)` columnwise) instead of TE's 128x4-padded shape. #3518 asks GEMM to accept such scales too (#3519). The quantize kernels, however, assumed the padded layout, so quantizing into compact buffers wrote outside them or produced wrong scales.

Reproduced on current `main` (`eb3c860`) on B200: the reporter's script prints `256 256` instead of `0 0`. A sweep over 9 shapes × FP32/BF16/FP16 inputs × rowwise/columnwise/both × 1D/2D scaling, plus E5M2, passed 53 of 180 cases. Compact views 1 or 4 bytes past 16-byte alignment raised `cudaErrorMisalignedAddress`. The FP8 data was always correct; the scales were wrong in three kernels:

| Kernel | Used for | Failure with compact scales |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generic `quantize_mxfp8_kernel` | FP32 input, 2D scaling, columnwise-only, partial tiles | Rowwise stores are bounded by column only and columnwise stores not at all. They write past the buffer when `rows % 64 != 0` and into the next scale row when `cols % 64 != 0`. |
| Staged bidimensional cast (`CastTraitsSwizzle`) | BF16/FP16, rowwise + columnwise | Rowwise scales are flushed in 4- or 8-byte groups, so rows that are not a multiple of four scales long are dropped or misplaced. Columnwise scales are stored for whole 64-column iterations. |
| Register-resident rowwise and bidimensional casts | BF16, `cols % 128 == 0` / `% 256 == 0` | 64- and 128-bit stores fault on views that are not 16-byte aligned. |

So BF16 inputs stay in bounds only for some shapes.

Review of the first commit found that views whose scale rows hold more entries than blocks also fail in the specialized kernels. The register-resident bidimensional kernel faults when columnwise scale rows are not a multiple of 16 bytes long. The rowwise-only kernels reject such rows (register-resident) or leave some of them unwritten (staged).

Fixes #3689

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Generic kernel: bound rowwise scale stores by the scale tensor's rows, and columnwise stores by its rows and columns. TE's padded tensors cover every chunk, so their stores are unchanged.
- Kernel selection: use the specialized kernels only when the scale pointers are 16-byte aligned, the rowwise scale stride is a multiple of four, rowwise-only casts write packed scale rows (one entry per block), and, for the staged bidimensional kernel, each columnwise scale row spans whole 64-column iterations. Other layouts use the generic kernel. The register-resident bidimensional kernel also needs columnwise scale rows that are a multiple of 16 bytes long; other row lengths take the staged kernel. TE's padded tensors always qualify, so their kernel selection is unchanged.
- Validation: reject unswizzled scale tensors that are not 2D or hold fewer than one scale per block, which would otherwise leave scales unwritten. GEMM-swizzled scales are not affected.
- Tests: `tests/pytorch/mxfp8/test_mxfp8_quantize_compact_scales.py` and `CompactScalesCastMXFP8TestSuite` in `tests/cpp/operator/test_cast_mxfp8.cu` quantize into compact views, and into views whose scale rows hold more entries than blocks. Canary bytes surround every view, and the views are aligned and unaligned. The tests compare the results byte for byte with TE's padded output. The C++ suite also covers FP16 input and the dbias variant.

GEMM's handling of compact scales (#3519) is unchanged.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

<details>
<summary>Testing on B200 (CUDA 13.1, PyTorch 2.11.0a0)</summary>

PyTorch-only editable build for `sm_100a` with `NVTE_WITH_NCCL_EP=0` and `NVTE_WITH_CUTEDSL=0`. Each run checked that the imported libraries came from this build.

| Check | `main` (`eb3c860`) | First commit (`9cae9e1`) | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reporter's script | `256 256` | `0 0` | `0 0` |
| Sweep with aligned / +4 B / +1 B views | 53/180 / misaligned address / misaligned address | 180/180 each | 180/180 each |
| PyTorch test: compact views, 218 cases | 174 failed | 218 passed | 218 passed |
| PyTorch test: longer scale rows, 108 cases | | 11 failed | 108 passed |
| C++ suite, 1008 cases | 130 of the first commit's 144 cases failed | 13 failed | 1008 passed |
| All suites in `test_cast_mxfp8` | | 940 passed, 488 skipped | 1804 passed, 488 skipped |
| `tests/pytorch/mxfp8` | | 665 passed, 1035 skipped | 773 passed, 1035 skipped |
| `test_mxfp8_2d_quantize.py` | | 135 passed | 135 passed |
| `test_quantized_tensor.py` | | 390 passed, 200 skipped | 390 passed, 200 skipped |
| `test_numerics.py -k mxfp8` | | 81 passed | 81 passed |
| `test_fusible_ops.py -k mxfp8` | | 364 passed, 445 skipped | 364 passed, 445 skipped |
| `test_weight_swizzle_in_layers.py` | | 52 passed | 52 passed |
| `test_partial_cast.py` | | 1 passed | 1 passed |

Not covered: JAX (not installed; JAX passes padded MXFP8 scales, which keep the same stores and kernels), the CuTeDSL backend (not built), and performance (not measured).

The C++ operator tests on `main` do not compile with CUDA 13.1. Since #3325, `DType::kFloat8UE5M3` exists for every CUDA version, but `TypeInfo::types` lists `fp8ue5m3` only for CUDA 13.4 and later. I built `test_cast_mxfp8.cu` against a local copy of `test_common.h` that ends the type lookup there; that workaround is not part of this PR.

</details>

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; the previous alignment issue is fixed and no new actionable issues were found.

Summary

Adds support for compact, unswizzled MXFP8 scale buffers. - MXFP8 quantization now writes scales into compact unswizzled buffers. The previous alignment finding is fixed. No new actionable issues were found. GPU tests were not run during this review. Reviews (2) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[Common\] Check MXFP8 scale row lengths b..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/097642fcbe1e6c7376fb1a34b100252216d30350) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

cc @vthumbe1503 

FYI, this PR looks a bit vibey but you might want to steer it?

I tested this PR on a B300 (sm_103). TE was built for `103a` from main `fac8d4a9`, once as-is and once with this PR's diff applied, both with CUDA 13.3.

The reproducer from #3689 counts the bytes written past the compact scale views, rowwise / columnwise:

| Shape | main | main + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| (32, 256) | 256 / 256 | 0 / 0 |
| (96, 128) | 128 / 128 | 0 / 0 |
| (64, 64) | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| (512, 96) | 0 / 32 | 0 / 0 |

The new `tests/pytorch/mxfp8/test_mxfp8_quantize_compact_scales.py` fails 282 of 326 cases on main and passes all 326 with this PR. The rest of `tests/pytorch/mxfp8/` also passes with this PR: 447 passed, 0 failed. The 1035 CuTe DSL backend cases were skipped in that environment.

I did not build or run the new C++ test (`tests/cpp/operator/test_cast_mxfp8.cu`).

Thanks for the PR. FYI, I have these 2 PRs in the works
https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3682/changes --> We have new optimized kernels for swizzling. And so the compact swizzling needs to be added for those kernels too

 https://github.com/vthumbe1503/TransformerEngine/pull/8 --> which has the changes from the previous PR + changes needed for swizzling to read from unpadded compact scales.

**Later scale rows remain unaligned** The new `scales_fit_specialized` check tests each buffer's base address, but not the alignment of later columnwise rows. A BF16 input shaped `(64, 256)`, with aligned rowwise scales shaped `(64, 8)` and columnwise scales shaped `(2, 257)`, passes these checks and selects `launch_cast_bidim`. That kernel keeps the 257-byte stride and issues an 8-byte store at the second row's unaligned address. Quantization can therefore still fail on an accepted layout. Check the columnwise stride against the selected kernel's store alignment, or send these layouts to the generic kernel.

Confirmed on B200. With BF16 (64, 256) input, (64, 8) rowwise scales and (2, 257) colwise scales, the register-resident bidimensional kernel faults with a misaligned address on the second colwise scale row.

The same check also missed rowwise-only casts into scale rows longer than one entry per block. `launch_cast_rowwise` rejects them, and the staged rowwise kernel leaves some of those rows unwritten, because its threads past the last column return before the scale flush.

Fixed in 097642fcbe1e6c7376fb1a34b100252216d30350:
- The register-resident bidimensional kernel now also requires colwise scale rows that are a multiple of 16 bytes long; other row lengths take the staged kernel.
- Rowwise-only casts into longer scale rows use the generic kernel.

Both the PyTorch and C++ tests now cover longer scale rows.

detail.title: [Common] Support compact unswizzled scales in MXFP8 quantization

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,179 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2022-2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+import transformer_engine.pytorch as te
+import transformer_engine_torch as tex
+from transformer_engine.pytorch import MXFP8Quantizer, MXFP8Tensor
+
+recipe_available, reason_for_no_recipe = te.is_mxfp8_available(return_reason=True)
+
+CANARY = 0xAA
+GUARD = 256  # Bytes on each side of a scale view that quantization must leave untouched.
+
+
+def _make_quantizer(rowwise, columnwise, with_2d_quantization):
+    quantizer = MXFP8Quantizer(
+        tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3,
+        rowwise=rowwise,
+        columnwise=columnwise,
+        with_2d_quantization=with_2d_quantization,
+    )
+    quantizer.optimize_for_gemm = False
+    return quantizer
+
+
+def _make_output(shape, scale_shapes, rowwise, columnwise, with_2d_quantization, scale_offset=0):
+    """MXFP8 tensor whose unswizzled scales are views guarded by canary bytes on both sides."""
+    guards = {}
+
+    def scale_view(name):
+        numel = scale_shapes[name][0] * scale_shapes[name][1]
+        start = GUARD + scale_offset
+        buf = torch.full((start + numel + GUARD,), CANARY, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        guards[name] = buf, start, numel
+        return buf[start : start + numel].view(scale_shapes[name])
+
+    def data():
+        return torch.empty(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+
+    out = MXFP8Tensor(
+        shape=shape,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device="cuda",
+        rowwise_data=data() if rowwise else None,
+        rowwise_scale_inv=scale_view("rowwise") if rowwise else None,
+        columnwise_data=data() if columnwise else None,
+        columnwise_scale_inv=scale_view("columnwise") if columnwise else None,
+        fp8_dtype=tex.DType.kFloat8E4M3,
+        quantizer=_make_quantizer(rowwise, columnwise, with_2d_quantization),
+        with_gemm_swizzled_scales=False,
+    )
+    return out, guards
+
+
+def _check_quantized(out, ref, guards, shape):
+    """Compare with TE's own quantization into padded scales, byte by byte.
+
+    Only the leading entry of each scale row per block is compared, and no byte around a
+    scale view may change.
+    """
+    rows, cols = shape
+    for name, (buf, start, numel) in guards.items():
+        outside = torch.cat([buf[:start], buf[start + numel :]])
+        assert torch.all(outside == CANARY), f"{name} scales were written outside their buffer"
+    if out._rowwise_data is not None:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out._rowwise_data, ref._rowwise_data, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            out._rowwise_scale_inv[:, : cols // 32],
+            ref._rowwise_scale_inv[:rows, : cols // 32],
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+    if out._columnwise_data is not None:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out._columnwise_data, ref._columnwise_data, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            out._columnwise_scale_inv[:, :cols],
+            ref._columnwise_scale_inv[: rows // 32, :cols],
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not recipe_available, reason=reason_for_no_recipe)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape",
+    # Row and column counts that are not multiples of the kernels' 64- and 128-element
+    # tiles, rows of fewer than four scales, and one scale per row or column block.
+    [(32, 256), (96, 128), (64, 64), (512, 96), (160, 224), (32, 32)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("usage", ["rowwise", "columnwise", "both"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_2d_quantization", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("scale_offset", [0, 4], ids=["aligned", "unaligned"])
+def test_quantize_into_compact_scales(shape, dtype, usage, with_2d_quantization, scale_offset):
+    """Compact unswizzled scales hold the same values as TE's padded scales.
+
+    Quantization must not write past either end of a compact scale buffer, which may be one
+    of several planes packed into a larger allocation.
+    """
+    rows, cols = shape
+    rowwise = usage in ("rowwise", "both")
+    columnwise = usage in ("columnwise", "both")
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    src = (8 * torch.randn(shape, device="cuda")).to(dtype)
+
+    ref = _make_quantizer(rowwise, columnwise, with_2d_quantization)(src)
+    out, guards = _make_output(
+        shape,
+        {"rowwise": (rows, cols // 32), "columnwise": (rows // 32, cols)},
+        rowwise,
+        columnwise,
+        with_2d_quantization,
+        scale_offset,
+    )
+    out.quantize_(src)
+    _check_quantized(out, ref, guards, shape)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not recipe_available, reason=reason_for_no_recipe)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "shape",
+    # Reach the register-resident rowwise and bidimensional kernels and the staged ones.
+    [(64, 128), (64, 256), (96, 384)],
+    ids=lambda shape: f"{shape[0]}x{shape[1]}",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float16], ids=lambda dtype: str(dtype)[6:]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("usage", ["rowwise", "columnwise", "both"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "extra",
+    # Scale entries per row beyond one per block, as (rowwise, columnwise).
+    [(0, 1), (4, 0), (4, 16), (1, 1)],
+    ids=lambda extra: f"extra{extra[0]}x{extra[1]}",
+)
+def test_quantize_into_pitched_scales(shape, dtype, usage, extra):
+    """Unswizzled scale rows may hold more entries than blocks, as in a padded view.
+
+    Whichever kernel runs, the leading entries hold the same values as TE's padded scales.
+    """
+    rows, cols = shape
+    rowwise = usage in ("rowwise", "both")
+    columnwise = usage in ("columnwise", "both")
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    src = (8 * torch.randn(shape, device="cuda")).to(dtype)
+
+    ref = _make_quantizer(rowwise, columnwise, False)(src)
+    out, guards = _make_output(
+        shape,
+        {
+            "rowwise": (rows, cols // 32 + extra[0]),
+            "columnwise": (rows // 32, cols + extra[1]),
+        },
+        rowwise,
+        columnwise,
+        with_2d_quantization=False,
+    )
+    out.quantize_(src)
+    _check_quantized(out, ref, guards, shape)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not recipe_available, reason=reason_for_no_recipe)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("usage", ["rowwise", "columnwise"])
+def test_quantize_rejects_undersized_scales(usage):
+    """Scales one block short of the tensor are rejected instead of being partially written."""

inline_comments.body: **Later scale rows remain unaligned** The new `scales_fit_specialized` check tests each buffer's base address, but not the alignment of later columnwise rows. A BF16 input shaped `(64, 256)`, with aligned rowwise scales shaped `(64, 8)` and columnwise scales shaped `(2, 257)`, passes these checks and selects `launch_cast_bidim`. That kernel keeps the 257-byte stride and issues an 8-byte store at the second row's unaligned address. Quantization can therefore still fail on an accepted layout. Check the columnwise stride against the selected kernel's store alignment, or send these layouts to the generic kernel.

inline_comments.body:
Confirmed on B200. With BF16 (64, 256) input, (64, 8) rowwise scales and (2, 257) colwise scales, the register-resident bidimensional kernel faults with a misaligned address on the second colwise scale row.

The same check also missed rowwise-only casts into scale rows longer than one entry per block. `launch_cast_rowwise` rejects them, and the staged rowwise kernel leaves some of those rows unwritten, because its threads past the last column return before the scale flush.

Fixed in 097642fcbe1e6c7376fb1a34b100252216d30350:
- The register-resident bidimensional kernel now also requires colwise scale rows that are a multiple of 16 bytes long; other row lengths take the staged kernel.
- Rowwise-only casts into longer scale rows use the generic kernel.

Both the PyTorch and C++ tests now cover longer scale rows.
